entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad, Lucknow Bench
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Heard learned counsel for the applicant as well as learned A.G.A. and perused the record.
2. In terms of the F.I.R., the applicant is not named in the F.I.R.
Subsequently, the name of the applicant surfaced in the statement of the co accused.

It is argued that in similar circumstances, one of the co accused Arshad @ Sanu who was also named in the F.I.R., has been granted bail vide order dated 23.5.2023 passed in Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.7638 of 2022.

entities.text: Crl. Misc. Bail Application No.7638 of 2022
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: The criminal history of the applicant has been duly explained in paragraph 19 of the bail application.
The applicant is in jail since 19.4.2022, hence the applicant may also be enlarged on bail on the ground of parity.
3. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail by arguing that a very serious offence has been committed by the accused applicant in the said case, but could not the deny the ground of parity.
Naveen Jaiswal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

entities.text: Naveen Jaiswal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. Considering the fact that the implication of the applicant is similar to that of the co accused Arshad @ Sanu who has already been granted bail by a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court coupled with the fact that the applicant is in custody since 19.4.2022 and there is nothing on record to demonstrate that the applicant if enlarged on bail, would in any way adversely affect the trial and without expressing any opinion on merit, I am of the view that the applicant is entitled to be released on bail on the ground of parity.
5. Accordingly, the bail application is allowed.

6. Let the applicant Naveen Jaiswal be released on bail in FIR/ Case Crime No.29 of 2022, under Sections 272, 302, 420, 467, 468, 471, 328, 120(B), 259, 260 I.P.C. and Section 60(A)/72 of the Excise Act, Section 63 of the Copyright Act, Police Station Maharajganj, District Raebareli on his furnishing personal bonds and two reliable sureties of Rs.25,000/- each to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions :-
(a) The applicant shall execute a bond to undertake to attend the hearings;
(b) The applicant shall not commit any offence similar to the offence of which he is accused or suspected of the commission; and (c) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade her from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
Order Date :- 17.1.2024 Shukla  Naveen Jaiswal vs State Of U.P. Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.
